Натрий Йокситаламат C12H10I3N2NaO5 = 665.9. CAS — 33954-26-6. ATC — V08AA05. ATC Vet — QV08AA05. Description. Sodium ioxitalamate contains about 57.2% of I. Profile Ioxitalamic acid is an ionic monomeric iodinated radiographic contrast medium (p.1474) with actions similar to those of the amidotrizoates (p.1475). It is given intravenously or by instilla- tion into body cavities for procedures including angiography, cholangiography, cystography, hysterosalpingography, and urography; it may be given orally or rectally for imaging of the gastrointestinal tract. It is also used for contrast enhancement in computed tomography. Ioxitalamic acid is usually available as a solution containing 21% of the sodium salt (equivalent to 120 mg/mL of iodine), 55.1 to 66% of the meglumine salt (equivalent to 250 to 300 mg/mL of iodine), or as a mixture of both salts. The dose and strength used vary according to the procedure and route. Monoethanolamine ioxitalamate has also been used.
